state:
- The supported-premise block places the Lagadinou, Farge, and Pollyea comparator findings beside the single positive Sykes premise, which inflates the apparent evidence that teriflunomide induces differentiation. Keep only the DHODH-to-myeloid-maturation result as a premise and move the ROS-low, cytarabine-residual, and venetoclax-azacitidine observations entirely into the alternative and discriminator sections.
- The falsifiers test differentiation only after DHODH is already engaged, so a drug that works solely at free levels above multiple-sclerosis exposure can still survive the preclinical kill criteria. Add an explicit translational falsifier: dihydroorotate accumulation and uridine/cytidine-nucleotide depletion must occur at unbound concentrations documented for the approved dose, and failure at that exposure falsifies the repurposing claim even if higher concentrations mature blasts.
- The validation plan leaves the xenograft readout, the maturation-versus-death time window, the control nucleoside, and the multi-sample decision rule unspecified, so a single marker shift or one responsive sample could be scored as confirmation. Predeclare sampling times in still-viable cells, name the non-rescuing nucleoside, define the PDX marrow maturation and burden endpoints against the venetoclax-azacitidine reference, and set the fraction of genetically distinct differentiation-arrested samples that must show uridine-rescuable maturation.
